newsitem.title: USA: Montana small grain crops benefit from needed rain.
newsitem.headline: Montana small grain crops benefit from needed rain.

text.p: Soil moisture conditions improved dramatically in Montana from a week ago, the state's Agricultural Statistics Service reported.
Statewide topsoil moisture was rated 7 percent short or very short, down from 44 percent a week earlier.
Winter wheat was headed on 95 percent of the acreage, unchanged from the five year average and 22 percent of the crop was turning color, compared with the 19 percent average.
Spring wheat was headed on 61 percent, up from an average of 45 percent.
Oats had headed on 56 percent of the acreage, up from a normal 43 percent while barley was headed on 54 percent, ahead of the average of 45 percent.
Although the rain was beneficial for grains, it held up hay harvesting. First alfalfa cutting was 43 percent complete, behind the average of 51 percent.
The rain helped pastures and ranges, which were rated 62 percent good to excellent, compared with 55 percent last week.
